analysis: The only change is a documentation row in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 397). It adds DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL: exact `0` disables, default on, read once per process, not forwarded to LaunchAgents. It governs the fused causal SDPA path for full-attention prompt chunks in libs/mlx-swift-lm AttentionV1.swift. I examined this against the threat model, including the T-041 prefix-cache and TTFT oracle, T-028 residual GPU data, and TB-007. The row is docs only and changes no code or trust-boundary behavior. It adds no environment passthrough, no network or auth surface, no persistence, and no change to the encrypted SSD cache's TTL, HMAC names, scope or gating. The documented performance toggle could change TTFT magnitudes, but that does not alter the accepted SEC-035 same-account timing channel in kind; the cache hit/miss oracle is independent of prefill kernel choice. The `libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../AttentionV1.swift` implementation and the architecture/inference.md anchor are outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify numerical equivalence or fallback behavior. The doc itself says the toggle is read once per process and not forwarded to LaunchAgents, which keeps the installed-provider default stable. I identified no security regression. The remaining question is whether the fused kernel path alters prefix-cache checkpoint or restore correctness; that belongs to the code change and is not visible here.
